newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Usinor profits dive, sees weaker H2.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Usinor profits dive, sees weaker H2.

text.p: Europe's largest steelmaker Usinor Sacilor, privatised last July, announced on Tuesday that first-half profits plunged by 65 percent and warned that its second half earnings would be even weaker.
Net attributable profit slumped to 833 million francs ($162.6 million) from 2.36 billion francs in the first half of 1995 and a record 4.43 billion franc profit in full year 1995.
Turnover fell to 37.39 billion francs from 41.63 billion.
Usinor's results were hammered by lower demand for steel as customers reduced their stocks because of oversupply in a weak economic environment.
It forecast the second half would be weaker than the first because of the seasonal nature of its business but would remain still "clearly positive".
Chairman Francis Mer later explained at a news conference that activity traditionally slows down in the second half of the year due to the summer and Christmas holidays.
But Mer predicted better earnings in the first half of 1997.
"All the conditions are there so that the first half of 1997 will show an improvement when compared to the mediocre (first half 1996) figure," he said.
Destocking limited demand for steel in the first half of 1996. But with destocking almost over, order books and prices are now on the rise.
But Mer cautioned 1997 would not be an easy year for the steel sector. "We are at the end of a disagreeable period but we are not at the beginning of a very sharp upturn," he said.
"It's obvious the year 1997 in our core sector (steel) will be a year of transition, a difficult year -- but it will be less difficult than 1996," he said.

Usinor shares plunged by some six percent on the profit fall announcement but then recovered to trade higher after the company forecast a better 1997 first half. In early afternoon it was up 2.53 percent or 1.90 francs at 77.0 francs.
The company was sold off to small investors at 86 francs per share.
The 10 percent drop in turnover from a year ago was due mainly to lower volumes. Loss-making long products unit Unimetal also heavily weighed on group performance in the first half.
Mer pegged losses incurred by Unimetal at "several hundred million francs" but predicted a better performance in 1997.
Group net debt at the first half stage totalled 8.35 billion francs compared to 11.04 billion at the end of 1995 and is expected to further decline in the second half of 1996.
Usinor also announced special steel unit Ascometal was launching a buyout offer for the remaining 32.7 percent capital of suspension components unit Allevard Industries that it does not already own.
The offer priced at 385 francs per share spells an investment of some 180 million francs and was expected to have a slightly positive impact on earnings per share, Mer said.
